verdicts.candidate: Deterministic Auto Send, the no AI control
verdicts.cost_of_error: Lowest in the set and self correcting. A wrong fire sends a duplicate text with form links, which a patient ignores and staff can see in a send log. No clinical content, no money determination, no irreversible action. The one real error mode is a text to a mistyped number, the same exposure ANHC's existing manual text already carries (C10). Who catches it, the intake staff who watch the same queue they watch today.
verdicts.data_readiness: The best in the set, and this is why it goes first. It needs one trigger on ANHC's own online registration form and one send through the SMS channel ANHC already operates (C10, C14). Neither touches the Epic MyChart instance operated for Providence Health and Services Alaska (C81), so the one unknown integration in the whole map is untouched. What does NOT exist is any baseline, no published figure for how many registrations stall or how long the loop actually takes, so the first deliverable is instrumentation, not a feature.
verdicts.step_math: Compounding does not apply. These are deterministic software steps at effectively 99.9 percent each, tested exhaustively against a fixed input set, not model calls at 85 to 90 percent. Four steps of rules is still four steps of rules. Stating a model style reliability number here would be dishonest in the pessimistic direction.
verdicts.change_or_reason: Keep exactly as scored, and keep the finding that it outscored every AI candidate at 5.95. One condition binds it and it is load bearing for the entire recommendation. NOTHING IN THE VERIFIED RECORD SAYS WHY the 1 to 2 business day window exists. C10 states the window, it does not state the cause. If a human verifies identity or checks for a duplicate chart before the links go out, then the window is a POLICY and instant auto send is unsafe, and the correct build is a same day service level with the check kept, not a zero second send. That question is answered in week one with ANHC's own staff before a line of code is written.

verdicts.cost_of_error: Split it, because the parts do not carry the same risk. Extraction into a sliding fee application is a money determination on a person who by definition may not be able to pay, so a wrong household size or income figure either overcharges someone at the edge of affording care or under charges in a way that becomes an HRSA sliding fee compliance problem. That is costly and unforgiving, so it requires human review on every filed form with no sampling exception. The mitigating fact is ANHC's own rule, a one year discount requires submitted documentation (C16), so the organization's existing policy already puts a human and a document between a model output and a final determination. The model can never be the determinant. Retrieval question answering carries a different and sharper risk, a patient asking a clinical question in an administrative channel, so the answerable set is an allowlist of published administrative topics and everything else refuses to the main line, 907-743-7200 (C14). Language carries the third risk and it is evidenced, C59 and C60 sit in one sentence.
verdicts.data_readiness: Three gaps and each one is scope, not a footnote. FIRST, the eval corpus does not exist. Field level extraction can't be accepted without a labeled set of historical completed intakes, de identified, stratified by language and by channel, and nobody has built it. Building and labeling that set IS the project's first month. SECOND, write access is UNKNOWN, not hard. C81 verifies only that ANHC's portal link resolves to an Epic MyChart login operated for Providence Health and Services Alaska, and the Epic Community Connect inference was explicitly killed, so no design may assume any write path. This build's answer is to need none, it hands staff a completed packet and staff book. THIRD, this is PHI. Household income, household size and dates of birth over SMS require a signed BAA with any model vendor, a written no training on our data term, and the same consent posture ANHC's existing text channel already carries.
verdicts.step_math: The honest count is TWO model steps, not twelve, and that is the entire reason this survives. Comprehend what the patient wrote in their own words, then propose candidate field values. At 90 percent per step a fully model completed packet lands near 81 percent first pass, at 95 percent near 90 percent. Add the allowlisted question answerer and it is three model touches on the worst case path, roughly 73 to 86 percent. Those are the numbers to put in the study, not a rounded accuracy claim. What matters more is where the error lands. One human gate sits before anything is filed, so the residual error reaching a filed application is the staff miss rate on a pre filled form, not the model rate. The honest cost of that design is that the gate consumes staff time, so the measured win is that reviewing a filled packet is faster than gathering one on a phone call. Any framing that counts the review as free is the freed hours error from the kill list.
verdicts.change_or_reason: Keep it, with three cuts, and the middle one contradicts the strategist directly. CUT ONE, the sliding fee trigger classifier is KILLED as an AI capability. All three triggers in C18 are computable. New patient at ANHC is a lookup for any ANHC encounter inside 36 months (C12). Before your discount expires is date math on an issue date plus twelve or six months (C16). A change in household size or annual income is a numeric comparison against the last application on file. That is arithmetic against records ANHC already keeps, so a model would be slower, more expensive and impossible to test exhaustively. It runs as plain code with unit tests, including a named test for the C17 edge case where a 30 day temporary self declaration usable once every twelve months leaves a patient with a twelve month tail and no cover. CUT TWO, runtime translation of anything the patient reads and acts on is KILLED. The four published forms (C19) are fixed documents, so translating them into more of the languages behind the homepage figure of 56 translated (C20) is a one time, human reviewed translation project that becomes a static file lookup. That is the LOOKUP rung, not the model rung. The model's language job shrinks to comprehending inbound free text for staff, never to generating patient facing instruction in an unreviewed language. CUT THREE, the question answerer is an allowlist of published administrative topics with a default deny, not a general assistant over the site, and it cites the page it answered from. One design requirement carries over from C63, where ambient scribes propagated interpreter errors into notes in simulated encounters. Every extracted field stores the patient's original text verbatim beside it, so a reviewer and any later auditor can see the source rather than a laundered version of it. NAMING HONESTY, this is a deterministic workflow with two supervised model steps. Calling it a concierge implies an autonomy it does not have and will not be given.

verdicts.cost_of_error: Moderate on the reminder, high on the determination. A wrong expiry date tells a patient to reapply when they need not, which wastes a visit and erodes trust in the channel. The reverse, a missed reminder, is the failure that costs money and it costs the patient, not ANHC. The determination side carries the same sliding fee exposure as the concierge and takes the same mandatory human gate. Who catches a wrong date, nobody, unless the engine is built to reconcile its own reminder log against the source discount record, which is a build requirement rather than an assumption.
verdicts.data_readiness: The rules are the cleanest evidence in the whole package, verbatim and unambiguous (C16, C17, C18). The DATA is the problem. The engine needs discount issue dates, prior declared household size and income, and encounter recency, and all of that lives in the practice management and record systems, where read access is not established anywhere in the verified record. NOTE CAREFULLY that a model does not rescue this. The gap is access, not intelligence, and an AI version of this build is blocked by exactly the same wall. One unknown also sizes the whole opportunity and is unresolved, whether ANHC already sends renewal reminders is not in the verified record, so the gap being closed could be most of the value or almost none of it. That is a week one discovery question, never a modeled assumption.
verdicts.step_math: Not applicable to the clock, which is deterministic date arithmetic and gets unit tests rather than a reliability estimate. The only model exposure is the shared free text to fields step, one step, and it inherits the concierge's gate rather than adding a second one.
verdicts.change_or_reason: Survives, relabeled honestly and moved BEHIND the concierge. This is a deterministic reminder and renewal engine that borrows one extraction step, not an AI build, and it should be sold as the cheap thing it is. It carries the strongest genuine cost of delay in the map because it has a real clock (C16, C17). It shares most of its plumbing with the recommended pick, so building the concierge first makes this second build small. It is second and not first for one reason, its value is unknown until the reminder question is answered, and the concierge's value rests on ANHC's own published process rather than on an unknown.

verdicts.cost_of_error: The HIGHEST in the candidate set, and asymmetric in a way that breaks the usual scoring. C78 names the exact failure, Providence's CMO talks about getting suicidal ideation to the top of the inbox. A false positive costs a staff member thirty seconds. A false negative on that class can cost a life. Under the AI scoping test this is the textbook case of errors that are costly and unforgiving, so a model may only ever ADD escalations, never withhold one, and it may never replace the human read of the queue.
verdicts.data_readiness: NOT READY, and this is the disqualifier rather than the model. No ANHC message volume exists anywhere in the verified record, so the pocket can't be sized, an error budget can't be set, and a false negative rate has no denominator to be measured against. There is also no labeled corpus of ANHC messages with urgency labels, and building one means clinical staff labeling real patient messages, which is a governance project with its own approvals. The one precedent is operator reported with no published measurement (C78), and the 18 day build figure is an operator claim carried by the outlet (C79). C65 is the relevant contrast, a community clinic may lack the data scientists on staff needed to implement AI.
verdicts.step_math: Four steps, classify, risk rank, draft, route, at 92 percent per step gives about 72 percent clean end to end. That number is the wrong lens. The only figure that decides this build is RECALL ON THE URGENT CLASS, and there is no data with which to estimate it, let alone accept it. A build whose single decisive metric can't be estimated before contract is not scoped.
verdicts.change_or_reason: Killed for this engagement, and the reason is evidence rather than ambition. It serves the job that scored 8, not the one that scored 14, ANHC already runs a text channel on that line so the marginal gain is triage quality rather than access, and its decisive safety metric can't be measured with anything that exists today. AGENT WASHING FLAG, calling this a digital employee is the Gartner pattern named in AI_SCOPING. It is a classifier plus a draft generator with a human on every outbound. If ANHC wants urgent flagging before that, the honest first answer is NOT AI. A keyword escalation list is exhaustively testable, reviewable by a safety committee, and free. A model earns a place only later, only as a union with those rules so it can add escalations and never remove them, and only once message volume and a labeled set exist.

verdicts.cost_of_error: High and public. This is the patient facing front door of a health center whose mission is care regardless of ability to pay (C09), serving a panel that includes 314 mobile clinic visits at shelters across Anchorage (C30) and a homepage figure of 56 languages translated (C20). A stalled or misrecognizing bot on the line a person calls in a bad week is brand damage that no dashboard catches, because the people it fails hang up and are never counted. NOBODY CATCHES THOSE ERRORS, which is the disqualifying property.
verdicts.data_readiness: The central capability has NO VERIFIED PATH. Booking requires write access to an Epic MyChart instance operated for Providence Health and Services Alaska (C81), and the Community Connect inference was explicitly killed, so the integration is an unknown rather than a hard fact and is not ANHC's alone to grant. Without the write, impact falls to 0.5 by the strategist's own scoring and the agent re routes the same callback it was meant to remove. There is also no call volume, no abandonment rate and no hold time for ANHC anywhere in the record, so the problem it targets is unmeasured.
verdicts.step_math: Six steps on a booking call, recognize, classify intent, fill slots, check policy, write the appointment, confirm back. At 90 percent per step that is about 53 percent end to end, at 95 percent about 74 percent. Latency compounds the same path, AI_SCOPING puts smooth under about 800ms with many production systems landing at 1400 to 1700ms, which callers feel as slow. A 53 to 74 percent completion rate on the front door of a safety net clinic is not a product.
verdicts.change_or_reason: Killed on evidence rather than on taste, though taste is also a reason to be suspicious of it. THIS IS THE PRODUCT OUR OWN SHOP OVER INDEXES ON, which is grounds to discount it further rather than less. Its only supporting analogue is a vendor press release quoting a named health center CEO with no independent audit, no before and after abandonment rate and no disclosed cost (C76, C77). That is real information, labeled as tier three evidence, and it is not a baseline for ANHC. Two things would revive it and both are measurements ANHC can take without buying anything, a measured abandonment and hold time baseline on 907-743-7200, and a written answer on scheduling write access. Until then, the honest first move on that line is not AI at all, it is published call reason routing and a callback offer.

recommended_pick.name: The new patient intake workflow, deterministic auto send and sliding fee clock first, two supervised model steps on top
recommended_pick.why_it_survives: It survives BECAUSE MOST OF IT IS NOT AI, and the parts that are, are two steps behind one human gate. Phase one is the no AI control that outscored everything, 5.95, firing the intake form links the moment a registration lands instead of within 1 to 2 business days (C10), on a fixed reminder ladder, measured against baselines pulled from ANHC's own logs in week one. That ships alone. Model work earns its place on top of a measured baseline or it does not get built. What remains for a model is a genuinely narrow band, comprehending what a patient writes in their own words and proposing candidate field values for the intake and sliding fee packet, so the second staff call becomes a booking call instead of a data gathering call (C11, C18), plus an allowlisted answerer over the narrow set of administrative questions ANHC already publishes. Four properties carry it past the gate. It needs NO WRITE ACCESS to anything, so the one unverified integration in the map (C81) is untouched by design. Its failure mode is TODAY, if extraction is refused or wrong the patient gets blank form links and the existing callback, which is the current process, so the build can degrade to status quo and never below it. It is TWO model steps, so the compounding math lands at roughly 81 to 90 percent first pass on a completed packet rather than the 36 to 60 percent a ten step agent would carry, and that number goes in the study as a number rather than as the word accurate. And the human gate it requires is one ANHC's own policy already imposes, since a one year discount requires submitted documentation (C16), so no model output is ever a final determination. EVALUATION IS STATEABLE. Acceptance is field level exact match against staff confirmed gold on a held out set, with the target agreed before the build rather than after, plus a separate and stricter target of 100 percent refusal on clinical intent measured against an adversarial set of clinical questions phrased administratively. The eval set is 200 to 300 historical completed intakes from ANHC's own records, de identified, stratified by language and by channel, labeled by the intake staff who do this work today, AND IT DOES NOT EXIST YET, so building it is the first month of the project rather than a hidden assumption. Human review is every packet before filing, no sampling. Fallback is the blank links and the callback. ONE THING THIS BUILD DOES NOT DO and must never be described as doing, it does not touch appointment supply. Nothing in the record says whether the two published windows are a communications constraint or a schedule capacity constraint, so no claim that it shortens the wait to be seen is supportable. Two constraints from the evidence bind delivery. Pricing may not be per clinician per seat (C64, C54). Delivery carries the integration work itself (C65), and that integration work is what a buyer like this is actually purchasing. Last and it outranks all of it, ANHC ALREADY RUNS AN AMBIENT AI DOCUMENTATION TOOL IN CLINICAL PRODUCTION, ahead of every Alaska FQHC peer checked (C34, C82, C83, C84).
recommended_pick.renamed_from: New Patient Intake Concierge, rescoped. Deterministic auto send and sliding fee clock first, with two supervised model steps on top
recommended_pick.rename_reason: Renamed by the showrunner acting on this agent's own honest_flags entry, which said 'Concierge implies an autonomy this build does not have and will not be given.' The room asked for the fix, so the fix was made rather than noted.

where_not_to_use_ai: The sliding fee clock, the three reapplication triggers and the instant send of the intake form links are rules, not AI, and we would not build them any other way. Whether an ANHC provider saw you inside 36 months is a lookup, whether your discount expires is a date plus twelve or six months, and whether your household size or income changed is this application's number compared with the last one on file. That is arithmetic against records ANHC already keeps, so a model would be slower, cost more per run, and can't be tested exhaustively, while plain code with unit tests can be. The four published sliding fee forms are fixed documents too, so getting them into more languages is a one time human reviewed translation that becomes a static file, never a model generating patient facing instructions at runtime. AI touches exactly two things in this build, reading what a patient writes in their own words and turning it into candidate values on a form, and answering a bounded list of questions ANHC already publishes, with a person confirming before anything is filed.
honest_flags: THE SINGLE LOAD BEARING UNKNOWN, and it sits under the cheapest and highest scoring part of the recommendation. C10 states that intake form links arrive within 1 to 2 business days. It does not state WHY. If a human verifies identity or checks for a duplicate chart in that window, the window is a POLICY and not a lag, instant auto send is unsafe, and the correct build is a same day service level with the check preserved. Nothing in 89 verified claims resolves this. It is question one in week one, asked of ANHC's own intake staff, before any code.

The strategist's third AI justification does not survive. Classifying which of the three sliding fee reapplication triggers applies (C18) is deterministic given data ANHC already holds, and it is cut from the AI scope. This is a direct disagreement with the pick as handed over, and the pick is better for it.

The language justification survives only in a much narrower form than proposed. Pre translating fixed forms is a lookup, not AI. C58's non inferiority finding covers written material and Spanish, while C59 and C60 sit in one sentence, and C61 found back translation retaining 36 to 76 percent of meaning for certain non European languages. Live spoken interpretation is a permanent non goal, per C62.

None of the three outcome metrics have a baseline anywhere in the public record. Median hours to forms returned, median hours to a confirmed appointment, and the share of registrations that never reach a booked appointment all have to be pulled from ANHC's own logs. If those logs do not carry the timestamps, measurement is itself the first build and the study must say so rather than assume instrumentation exists.

A text and web build structurally excludes the population reached by 314 mobile clinic visits at shelters across Anchorage (C30), people who by definition may lack a stable number or device. That is a design constraint and it is also a measurement integrity risk, because the completion metric can improve while the hardest to reach patients are untouched. Report the metric split by channel or it will flatter the build.

Intake data is PHI. A signed BAA, a written no training on our data term, and the consent posture for income and household information over SMS are scope items with real elapsed time, not paperwork to handle later. C81 verifies only that the portal link resolves to an Epic MyChart login operated for Providence Health and Services Alaska, so a third party's data governance may also sit in the path and that has to be asked rather than assumed.

Two naming honesty calls. Concierge implies an autonomy this build does not have, it is a deterministic workflow with two supervised model steps. Digital employee, applied to the killed message triage build, is the agent washing pattern Gartner names.

The human review gate is NOT FREE. Staff time to review a pre filled packet is a real cost and counting the saved gathering time as pure gain would be the freed hours error from the kill list. The honest comparison to measure is review time against today's data gathering call, not against zero.

Two items ride to the roadmap rather than to the bin, and both are honest deferrals rather than dismissals. The coverage continuity engine carries the best cost of delay argument in the map and is blocked on one unanswered question, whether ANHC already sends renewal reminders. The interpreter error finding (C63) is advisory work, a sampling audit and a governance artifact, and it is worth saying plainly that the study is simulated rather than live clinical and that the absence of a public governance document is not evidence that no governance exists at ANHC.
